articles.title: How to Reduce AI API Costs by 40% Without Sacrificing Quality
articles.excerpt: When I first started integrating AI APIs into our production systems, I thought the hardest part would be prompt engineering or handling rate limits. I was wrong. The real challenge? Watching our mont…
articles.body: When I first started integrating AI APIs into our production systems, I thought the hardest part would be prompt engineering or handling rate limits. I was wrong. The real challenge? Watching our monthly bill climb from $200 to $2,000 in six weeks. If you're building with GPT-4, Claude, or Gemini, you've probably felt this pain. The good news? After months of testing and optimization, we've managed to cut our API costs by 40-50% without compromising output quality. Here's exactly how we did it. The Real Cost Problem Nobody Talks About Most developers focus on per-token pricing when comparing APIs. That's a mistake. The actual cost driver isn't the price per token—it's how many tokens you're burning through unnecessarily.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Tab Hibernator Sloth 🦥 - Save RAM Without Closing Tabs Chrome eats RAM when you keep 30+ tabs open. Closing them loses context, shopping carts, and research. Sloth doesn't close your tabs — it hibernates them. Tabs stay in your tab bar, turn faded, show as sleeping, use 0 RAM, and wake instantly when you click. One click to hibernate 25 tabs = ~1125MB saved. Built for everyone with 20+ tabs open. So, everyone: For developers: GitHub issues, Stack Overflow, localhost, docs - keep them all. Hibernate when you switch branches. 15 tabs = ~675MB back. For researchers & students: 20 papers, Notion, Drive, Medium articles. Don't close, hibernate. Export as Markdown for weekly review.

articles.title: The Two Hour Audit I Do Before Letting an Agent Touch Real Files
articles.excerpt: Last spring I let an agent run unsupervised in a real project directory for the first time. It finished the task I gave it, then kept making changes it thought were helpful, and one of those changes o…
articles.body: Last spring I let an agent run unsupervised in a real project directory for the first time. It finished the task I gave it, then kept making changes it thought were helpful, and one of those changes overwrote a config file I had spent a week tuning. Nothing was deleted. Nothing looked broken until the next morning. I lost two days rebuilding numbers I had never written down. That was the cheap version of the story. So now there is a two hour audit before any agent's first real run. Not because I assume it is hostile or incompetent. Because the first unattended run is the only run where I genuinely do not know the shape of the damage, and the price of learning it by accident is a config file, a database index, or a directory of half-written documents. The audit is deliberately boring.

articles.title: How LLM Context Works: Messages, Reasoning, and Tool Calls
articles.excerpt: Over the past week, I’ve been building the Agent Glossary, collecting fundamental terms that explain how LLMs work and how their capabilities relate to the context items they consume and produce. Let’…
articles.body: Over the past week, I’ve been building the Agent Glossary, collecting fundamental terms that explain how LLMs work and how their capabilities relate to the context items they consume and produce. Let’s walk through these terms one by one. Model A model is a trained AI system that generates content from the context it receives. In agent systems, it consumes context items, such as instructions, user messages, and tool outputs, and produces new items, such as model answers and tool calls. Most modern language models use the Transformer architecture. Their capabilities determine which context items they can consume and produce, and how those items are delivered: Tool calling enables the model to produce tool call items containing a function name and arguments.

articles.title: REA: a reverse engineering MCP for coding agents, tested with Ghidra and Electron
articles.excerpt: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and command-line interface (CLI) that gives your coding agent reverse engineering tools: decompile binaries with Ghidra, Hopper…
articles.body: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and command-line interface (CLI) that gives your coding agent reverse engineering tools: decompile binaries with Ghidra, Hopper or IDA, rebuild Electron apps, read .NET assemblies and observe websites. It installs from the rea-agents npm package, is MIT-licensed and is maintained by the morluto GitHub account. I tested it on 18 October 2026 in an arm64 Docker container with rea-agents 6.7.0, Node.js 24.21.0 and Ghidra 12.1.4. Here is what worked, what it weighs and what to check before you let it touch your agents’ configuration. The Spanish version is also available. Key takeaways rea-agents 6.7.0 exposes 207 MCP tools and 6 prompts, and its CLI has 153 commands.

articles.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
articles.excerpt: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered inter…
articles.body: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales. The sticking points Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not.

articles.title: Red Rising Is Officially Returning In 2027
articles.excerpt: A digital adaptation of Pierce Brown's beloved sci-fi saga is on its way.
articles.body: In the early 2010s, The Hunger Games captivated a generation, and in its wake came another dystopian tale set in the stars. Red Rising , a six-book saga by author Pierce Brown, traded the death-match arena for Mars, where a rigid, color-coded class system dictates daily life on the Red Planet. "Golds" are the most elite nenbers of Mars society, and they rule over the other colored classes, including the lowest class, "Reds." Much like Katniss Everdeen became the face of a revolution in The Hunger Games , Darrow, a lowborn "Red" miner, becomes the face of Red Rising's revolution.

articles.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: SpaceX will try to recover both Starship stages during the megarocket's next test flight, which is expected to take place in November, according to Elon Musk.
articles.body: SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle.

articles.body: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status.
